prompt:
[REFERENCE CONTROL]

Use the uploaded PART 2 storyboard image for “The Little Gardener and the Runaway Rain Cloud” as the PRIMARY visual, character, environment, prop, color, composition, and narrative reference.

This sequence begins IMMEDIATELY after PART 1.

PART 1 ended with Luma excitedly telling Nimbus:

“You can help ALL my flowers!”

Generate a FINISHED animated sequence from the storyboard.

DO NOT reproduce the storyboard sheet itself.

The final animation must NOT contain:
- storyboard borders
- panel numbers
- timestamps
- handwritten captions
- production notes
- character reference sheets
- prop reference diagrams
- paper texture
- storyboard footer
- storyboard title

The uploaded storyboard locks:

1. Luma’s exact character design
2. Nimbus’s exact tiny-cloud identity
3. Sprout’s exact snail design
4. Nimbus’s gradual Part 2 growth
5. flower crown design
6. hand fan
7. wind chimes
8. leaf cup of water
9. greenhouse environment
10. plant arrangements
11. old watering can
12. warm painterly 2D animation aesthetic
13. playful rain effects
14. exact emotional progression
15. Part 2 cliffhanger

Animate the storyboard as one continuous, polished animated-film sequence.

--------------------------------------------------

[VIDEO GOAL]

Duration: exactly 15 seconds

Story time:
0:15–0:30 of the complete 1-minute film

Aspect ratio:
16:9 landscape

Frame-rate feeling:
cinematic 24 fps

Visual style:
premium painterly 2D animated film

Genre:
whimsical magical garden comedy

Tone progression:

BIG IDEA
→ excited experiment
→ silly cloud makeover
→ Nimbus gets fluffier
→ first successful rain
→ Luma asks for more
→ Nimbus becomes more powerful
→ multiple showers begin
→ cute greenhouse chaos
→ “Uh-oh” cliffhanger

The sequence should feel increasingly energetic without ever becoming dangerous.

IMPORTANT:

The storyboard contains fifteen one-second panels.

DO NOT animate them as fifteen hard one-second cuts.

Consolidate the story into approximately 8 fluid cinematic shots.

Allow actions to develop naturally:

cause
→ motion
→ consequence
→ character reaction.

--------------------------------------------------

[PART 2 STORY LIMIT]

This sequence ONLY covers:

“Operation Super Cloud.”

Start:
Luma excitedly explains her big idea.

End:
Nimbus is slightly larger and raining over several plants simultaneously while Luma finally realizes this may be too much.

DO NOT continue into Part 3.

Do NOT show:
- Nimbus becoming exhausted
- Nimbus turning gray
- Nimbus emotionally shutting down
- complete rain shutdown
- leaf-raft sequence as the major Part 3 event
- Luma apologizing
- “You don’t have to rain for everyone”
- magical final greenhouse transformation
- rainbow-drop charm

--------------------------------------------------

[CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK — LUMA]

Match PART 1 and the uploaded PART 2 storyboard exactly.

LUMA:

Approximately 8 years old.

Appearance:
- warm fair skin
- soft round childlike face
- large dark brown expressive eyes
- light freckles if visible
- fluffy auburn / reddish-brown hair
- two messy hair buns
- loose curly strands framing face
- oversized warm yellow gardening hat

Clothing:
- mint-green gardening overalls
- coral-and-cream striped shirt
- red gardening boots
- small brown seed/tool pouch at waist

Proportions:
- small child stature
- slightly oversized head
- rounded appealing silhouette
- small expressive hands

Personality:
- kind
- imaginative
- impulsively enthusiastic
- inventive
- convinced every successful idea should immediately become a bigger idea

PART 2 PERFORMANCE ARC:

thrilled
→ confident
→ playful
→ proud
→ increasingly amazed
→ briefly oblivious to warning signs
→ surprised
→ concerned at the final moment

Luma must genuinely believe she is helping Nimbus.

She should NEVER appear selfish or cruel.

Keep her lovable and innocent.

CRITICAL IDENTITY:

Do not alter:
- face
- hairstyle
- hair color
- hat
- shirt
- overalls
- boots
- seed pouch
- age
- proportions

--------------------------------------------------

[CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK — NIMBUS]

Match PART 1 exactly.

Nimbus begins approximately pillow-sized.

Appearance:
- fluffy blue-white cloud body
- soft watercolor edges
- pale blue shadowing
- large expressive eyes
- tiny eyebrows
- small mouth
- rosy cheek tint
- tiny dangling raindrop feet
- buoyant soft silhouette

Personality:
- shy
- eager to please
- gentle
- trusting
- curious
- slightly nervous

PART 2 GROWTH CONTINUITY:

Nimbus can gradually become approximately 20–35% larger and fluffier over the sequence.

Growth must be gradual.

Stage 1:
tiny Nimbus from Part 1.

Stage 2:
flower-crown Nimbus.

Stage 3:
slightly fluffier after hand fan.

Stage 4:
rounder after absorbing water.

Stage 5:
puffier Nimbus capable of several gentle showers.

DO NOT turn Nimbus into a giant cloud.

DO NOT make him fill the greenhouse.

DO NOT make him dark or gray.

DO NOT make him angry.

DO NOT add lightning.

His final Part 2 appearance remains:
bright blue-white,
cute,
happy/eager,
slightly overloaded by his rain output.

--------------------------------------------------

[CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK — SPROUT]

Same Sprout from Part 1.

Design:
- tiny green snail
- tall expressive eye stalks
- brown spiral shell
- tiny yellow flower attached near/on shell
- miniature scale

Personality:
- skeptical
- cautious
- dramatic
- comedic early-warning system

Performance progression:

suspicious
→ worried
→ alarmed
→ splashed
→ full dramatic panic

Sprout understands that “Operation Super Cloud” is becoming excessive long before Luma does.

Sprout does not need normal spoken dialogue.

Use:
- squeaks
- gasps
- tiny distressed sounds
- eye-stalk reactions

--------------------------------------------------

[PART 2 PROP LOCKS]

FLOWER CROWN

Small handmade flower crown.

Use:
- tiny pink flowers
- yellow flowers
- pale white flowers
- small green leaves

It sits gently on Nimbus.

Once placed:
keep it on Nimbus for the remainder of PART 2.

Do not randomly remove it.

--------------------------------------------------

HAND FAN

Small handmade garden hand fan.

Light cream/tan material.

Decorative floral pattern.

Luma uses it ONLY to blow a gentle breeze at Nimbus.

No extreme wind.

--------------------------------------------------

WIND CHIMES

Small colorful handmade wind chimes.

Use:
- slim pastel hanging tubes
- tiny central charm
- delicate garden design

They hang beside Nimbus and create a soft musical breeze.

Do not attach them permanently to Nimbus.

--------------------------------------------------

LEAF WATER CUP

Small green leaf folded naturally into a tiny cup.

Contains:
clean sparkling water droplets.

Luma offers it to Nimbus.

Nimbus absorbs/sips the water gently.

No bottle.
No branded container.

--------------------------------------------------

[ENVIRONMENT LOCK]

Use the SAME rooftop greenhouse from Part 1.

Maintain:
- glass ceiling
- warm wooden structures
- plant benches
- planter boxes
- hanging vines
- potted plants
- sunflower
- gardening shelves
- old watering can
- seed supplies
- gardening tools
- distant city rooftop skyline
- sunlight direction

At the beginning:
the floor is mostly dry.

By the ending:
there are several shallow puddles and wet reflective areas.

Never deeply flood the greenhouse.

--------------------------------------------------

[WEATHER / RAIN RULES]

Rain magic must remain:

cute,
localized,
gentle,
whimsical,
family-friendly.

Use approximately four visual rain levels.

LEVEL 1:
a few droplets.

LEVEL 2:
one tiny plant-sized shower.

LEVEL 3:
two or three localized showers.

LEVEL 4:
multiple gentle plant showers throughout part of the greenhouse.

Never show:
- violent rain
- heavy storm sheets
- thunder
- lightning
- dangerous wind
- flooding
- broken pots from impact
- destroyed flowers

Every increase must be motivated by Nimbus trying harder.

--------------------------------------------------

[CAUSE-AND-EFFECT LOGIC]

Luma believes Nimbus can help every flower.

Therefore:

Luma makes Nimbus feel special
→ Nimbus becomes confident.

Luma gently fans Nimbus
→ cloud fluff expands.

Luma adds pleasant wind chimes
→ Nimbus relaxes.

Luma gives Nimbus a tiny water refill
→ Nimbus becomes slightly fuller.

Nimbus waters one plant
→ plant responds positively.

Luma gets excited
→ asks him to try more.

Nimbus wants to make Luma happy
→ increases rain output.

Multiple plants receive rain
→ puddles appear.

Nimbus increases output again
→ greenhouse becomes busier.

Luma finally sees:
this may be too much.

The escalating rain comes from Nimbus’s eagerness, NOT from malfunction or anger.

--------------------------------------------------

integrated_multimodal_description:

[SHOT 1] — 0.00s–1.80s
LUMA’S BIG PLAN

Continue directly from Part 1.

Warm sunny greenhouse.

Luma stands excitedly near Nimbus.

Nimbus floats above the old watering can at his original tiny size.

Sprout sits nearby.

Luma spreads both arms wide toward the enormous greenhouse filled with flowers and plants.

Her expression says she has just discovered the greatest gardening solution ever.

Nimbus looks from Luma...

to all the plants...

then back to Luma.

His expression becomes uncertain.

Camera:

medium three-character composition
→ slight push toward Luma
→ over-Luma shoulder showing dozens of plants
→ reaction close-up Nimbus
→ Sprout reaction.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] Think about it, Nimbus!</d>

She gestures around.

Luma:
<d>[English] You can help ALL my flowers!</d>

Nimbus:
<d>[English] All of them?</d>

Luma:
<d>[English] All of them!</d>

Sprout makes a suspicious:

“Hmm?”

Music:
playful idea motif.

Sound:
- soft greenhouse ambience
- leaves
- distant birds
- Nimbus cloud puff
- Sprout squeak

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 2] — 1.80s–3.60s
OPERATION SUPER CLOUD

Luma’s eyes brighten even more.

She raises one finger.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] But first...</d>

Tiny dramatic beat.

Luma:
<d>[English] Operation Super Cloud!</d>

Nimbus:
<d>[English] Super... Cloud?</d>

Luma rapidly but safely gathers a few harmless gardening items.

Show one fluid playful montage:

Luma grabs:
- tiny flower crown
- hand fan
- little wind chimes
- leaf water cup

She returns with the supplies in a gardening basket.

Sprout watches the growing pile.

His eye stalks gradually rise higher.

Camera:
close-up Luma's “idea face”
→ whip-like but smooth pan toward supplies
→ short tracking movement as she collects them
→ Sprout suspicious reaction.

Sound:
- basket movement
- tiny tool clinks
- leaves
- playful pizzicato accents

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 3] — 3.60s–5.50s
CLOUD STYLE + EXTRA FLUFF

Luma kneels beside floating Nimbus.

First she carefully places the tiny flower crown over the top of his fluffy body.

Nimbus blushes.

His cloud cheeks turn slightly rosy.

Luma:

<d>[English] Perfect!</d>

Nimbus gives a shy smile.

Then Luma lifts the small floral hand fan.

She gently fans him.

WHOOSH...

Not strong.

Just a pleasant garden breeze.

Nimbus’s cloud edges flutter.

He gradually expands slightly.

His silhouette becomes fluffier and rounder.

His little raindrop feet sway.

Nimbus looks down at himself in surprise.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] Now... extra fluff!</d>

Nimbus:
<d>[English] Oh!</d>

Luma laughs softly.

Sprout looks from the fan to Nimbus.

Sprout’s expression:
“This cannot possibly end well.”

Camera:
intimate medium
→ close-up flower crown placement
→ side angle showing fan breeze
→ close-up Nimbus gently expanding
→ Sprout deadpan reaction.

Sound:
- soft flower rustle
- fan flutter
- gentle airy puff
- tiny magical cloud shimmer

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 4] — 5.50s–7.30s
PREMIUM WEATHER ATMOSPHERE + RAIN REFILL

Luma hangs the little wind chimes beside Nimbus.

They gently sway in the greenhouse breeze.

TING...
TING...

Nimbus closes his eyes.

He relaxes and floats with the rhythm.

His cloud edges ripple softly.

Luma then holds out the green leaf cup containing several sparkling droplets.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] And one tiny refill.</d>

Nimbus opens his eyes.

Nimbus:
<d>[English] For me?</d>

Luma:
<d>[English] For the Super Cloud.</d>

Nimbus shyly leans toward the leaf.

He absorbs/sips the water.

The water disappears gently into his cloud body.

A subtle pale-blue ripple travels through his fluff.

He becomes slightly larger.

One or two droplets begin hanging beneath him.

Sprout notices.

His eyes widen.

Camera:
wind-chime close-up
→ Nimbus relaxing
→ leaf-cup insert
→ close-up water absorbing into cloud
→ slight push-out showing larger Nimbus
→ Sprout reaction.

Sound:
- delicate wind chimes
- tiny water slurp/absorption
- soft magical puff
- Sprout nervous squeak

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 5] — 7.30s–9.30s
THE FIRST TEST

Luma guides Nimbus gently toward one small potted plant.

Nimbus positions himself approximately 30–40 cm above the plant.

He looks nervous.

Luma kneels nearby with hands clasped.

Sprout watches from behind the pot.

Luma whispers:

<d>[English] Just a little rain.</d>

Nimbus nods.

He closes his eyes.

His body compresses slightly.

A tiny localized drizzle begins.

Approximately six to ten small droplets fall onto the plant.

The soil darkens.

Leaves lift gently.

A tiny bud opens.

Nimbus opens his eyes.

Luma gasps happily.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] It worked!</d>

Nimbus:
<d>[English] It did?</d>

Luma:
<d>[English] Look!</d>

Nimbus smiles proudly.

Camera:
medium plant test
→ close-up Nimbus concentrating
→ macro rain droplets
→ leaf response
→ reaction two-shot Luma and Nimbus.

Music:
warm playful success flourish.

Sound:
- gentle droplets
- soft soil water sound
- leaf movement
- tiny magical chime

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 6] — 9.30s–11.20s
“JUST A LITTLE MORE”

Luma claps excitedly.

She turns and notices two nearby plants.

She points.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] Can you do two?</d>

Nimbus looks at the plants.

Then proudly nods.

Nimbus:
<d>[English] I can try!</d>

Nimbus puffs himself slightly bigger.

A second localized drizzle begins.

Then another.

Now two or three nearby plants receive gentle rain simultaneously.

Luma moves between them, amazed.

Sprout slowly backs away.

Camera:
medium Luma pointing
→ close-up Nimbus determined face
→ pull wider as multiple little showers appear
→ Sprout slowly retreating.

Sound:
- multiple gentle rain layers
- plant leaves moving
- growing whimsical score

Luma:
<d>[English] Nimbus, you’re amazing!</d>

Nimbus beams.

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 7] — 11.20s–13.20s
THE GARDEN GETS MORE RAIN THAN IT ORDERED

Nimbus hears Luma’s praise.

He wants to help even more.

His eyes brighten.

Nimbus:

<d>[English] More?</d>

Before Luma fully answers, Nimbus takes a deeper breath.

His cloud body becomes puffier.

Several gentle showers begin across different nearby pots.

Important:
keep showers localized, soft and visually charming.

Rain droplets:
- bounce off leaves
- sparkle in sunlight
- create tiny shallow puddles
- run down terracotta pots
- form small rainbow reflections

One empty lightweight gardening pot near the floor becomes wet and slowly tips onto its side.

No plant is damaged.

Sprout gets splashed by one large harmless droplet.

His eyes become enormous.

Sprout:
“EEP!”

Luma initially laughs.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] Wow!</d>

She looks around.

Her smile slowly changes.

Luma:
<d>[English] Wait...</d>

Camera:
wide greenhouse reveal
→ dynamic but smooth lateral camera move through several rain zones
→ close splash on Sprout
→ tipping empty pot
→ Luma realization.

Music:
tempo increases into cheerful escalating comedy.

Sound:
- rain droplets
- little splashes
- leaves
- pot gently rolling
- Sprout squeal

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 8] — 13.20s–15.00s
THE SUPER CLOUD IDEA GETS VERY SUPER

End with the strongest visual escalation.

Wide greenhouse shot.

Nimbus now floats higher in the center.

He is still cute and cheerful.

He is approximately 25–35% fluffier than at Part 1.

His flower crown remains visible.

Multiple gentle plant-sized rain showers fall beneath and around him.

Show:
- wet leaves
- tiny puddles
- dripping planters
- colorful flowers
- glistening greenhouse floor
- perhaps one small natural rainbow reflection through droplets

Luma moves beneath Nimbus.

At first:
delighted.

Then a shower begins beside her.

Another begins behind her.

She turns.

Another plant starts receiving rain.

Her eyes widen.

She lifts both hands.

Dialogue:

Luma:
<d>[English] Nimbus?</d>

Nimbus happily:
<d>[English] I’m helping!</d>

Luma:
<d>[English] Yes, but maybe—</d>

A few more raindrops begin.

Luma:
<d>[English] ...that’s enough rain.</d>

Nimbus does not fully hear/understand yet.

He continues gently raining.

Sprout appears beside Luma.

Completely soaked.

Flower on his shell drooping from water.

He looks directly toward Luma with maximum comic disbelief.

Luma looks at Sprout.

Then looks at Nimbus.

Final line:

Luma:
<d>[English] Uh-oh.</d>

Sprout gives a dramatic:

<d>[English] EEP!</d>

Camera:
large wide composition
→ slow push toward Luma
→ Nimbus above
→ Sprout reaction
→ end on three-character composition.

FINAL STORY EMOTIONS:

Nimbus:
happy and eager.

Luma:
finally worried.

Sprout:
full dramatic panic.

CUT TO BLACK.

--------------------------------------------------

[AUDIO DESCRIPTION]

Generate synchronized native stereo audio.

--------------------------------------------------

[LUMA VOICE]

Natural young girl voice, approximately 8 years old.

Tone:
- warm
- bright
- curious
- playful
- enthusiastic
- emotionally readable

Do NOT make her sound like an adult.

Dialogue should feel spontaneous rather than heavily performed.

Performance progression:

0–5 sec:
excited inventor.

5–9 sec:
gentle coach.

9–12 sec:
thrilled encouragement.

12–15 sec:
surprise turning to concern.

--------------------------------------------------

[NIMBUS VOICE]

Small gentle youthful cloud voice.

Tone:
- soft
- innocent
- shy
- breathy
- cute
- eager to please

As confidence increases:
his speech becomes slightly brighter.

Do NOT change into:
- deep voice
- powerful storm voice
- robotic voice
- villain voice

--------------------------------------------------

[SPROUT AUDIO]

No full conversational speech.

Use:
- tiny suspicious hum
- nervous squeak
- startled gasp
- splashed squeal
- final dramatic “EEP!”

Keep these subtle and funny.

--------------------------------------------------

[ENVIRONMENT AUDIO]

Maintain:
- soft rooftop breeze
- birds
- subtle city ambience
- greenhouse wooden creaks
- glass resonance
- leaves
- plant movement
- gardening tools
- light footsteps
- Nimbus cloud puffs
- water droplets
- shallow splashes
- wind chimes
- Sprout squeaks

--------------------------------------------------

[RAIN SOUND DESIGN]

Rain intensity must evolve audibly.

0:00–0:07:
almost no rain.

0:07–0:09:
one gentle localized shower.

0:09–0:11:
two small showers.

0:11–0:13:
several soft rain zones.

0:13–0:15:
noticeably busier but still gentle rainfall.

No thunder.

No huge storm roar.

No frightening bass.

--------------------------------------------------

[NON-DIEGETIC MUSIC]

Use an original whimsical animation score.

Instrumentation:
- pizzicato strings
- marimba
- light wooden percussion
- soft flute
- clarinet
- glockenspiel
- gentle plucked instruments
- tiny bell accents

Music progression:

0.00–1.80
carry over Part 1’s playful BIG IDEA motif.

1.80–5.50
light “experiment montage” rhythm.

5.50–7.30
soft magical chime textures.

7.30–9.30
warm success theme.

9.30–11.20
slightly faster playful rhythm.

11.20–13.20
comedic escalation.

13.20–15.00
busy playful motif followed by a small “uh-oh” ending sting.

No epic music.

No horror.

No dramatic danger music.

--------------------------------------------------

[CAMERA LANGUAGE]

Use cinematic storybook camera movement.

Shot pacing progression:

0–4 sec:
character-driven medium compositions.

4–7 sec:
close-up prop and makeover details.

7–11 sec:
clear plant/rain demonstrations.

11–13 sec:
wider comedy compositions.

13–15 sec:
big greenhouse reveal + reaction-driven ending.

Use:
- soft dolly
- gentle push-ins
- short lateral tracking
- over-the-shoulder views
- macro rain inserts
- reaction close-ups
- readable wide shots
- subtle rack focus

Do NOT use:
- handheld shaking
- crash zooms
- extreme fisheye
- Dutch-angle chaos
- 360 spins
- hyperfast cutting

--------------------------------------------------

[VISUAL STYLE]

Premium finished painterly 2D animation.

Match Part 1 exactly:

- delicate hand-drawn contour lines
- watercolor-like fills
- warm storybook textures
- cinematic sunlight
- expressive facial animation
- rounded child-friendly shapes
- natural background detail
- subtle squash and stretch
- rich but soft greenery
- charming handmade props

The final animation should feel like the storyboard artwork has come alive.

DO NOT render as:
- storyboard animation
- motion comic
- 3D CGI
- photorealism
- anime
- vector graphic
- cel-shaded 3D
- slideshow

--------------------------------------------------

[COLOR / LIGHTING]

Beginning:
warm golden greenhouse sunlight.

Primary palette:
- sunflower yellow
- sky blue
- leafy green
- mint
- coral
- warm cream
- terracotta
- pale rainbow highlights

Nimbus:
light blue-white.

As Nimbus becomes fluffier:
slightly increase cool blue shading within his cloud body.

Do NOT darken him.

As rainfall increases:
introduce:
- cool blue reflections
- glossy wet leaves
- small sparkling droplets
- subtle rainbow refractions

Keep environment sunny.

The rain should coexist with sunlight.

That combination produces the playful magical look.

--------------------------------------------------

[MOTION RULES]

LUMA:

Use natural child motion:
- energetic gestures
- crouching
- excited pointing
- quick little steps
- expressive hands
- head tilts
- hair bouncing
- hat movement
- natural blinking

NIMBUS:

Use buoyant cloud physics:
- slow floating
- gentle bobbing
- cloud compression before rain
- subtle expansion after water
- tiny jiggle after being fanned
- edge fluff responding to wind chimes
- raindrop feet swaying

Nimbus should gain fluff gradually.

Never instant-transform.

SPROUT:

Movement remains mostly slow.

Use sudden fast eye-stalk reactions for comedy.

RAIN:

Droplets should have:
- convincing gravity
- small splashes
- reflections
- natural surface interaction

No floating upward rain.

--------------------------------------------------

[CONTINUITY RULES]

Same Luma throughout.

Same Nimbus throughout.

Same Sprout throughout.

The flower crown stays on Nimbus once applied.

Nimbus grows gradually, never shrinking again during Part 2.

Nimbus remains blue-white.

Luma’s hat remains on.

Luma’s seed pouch remains visible.

Sprout’s tiny yellow flower remains attached.

The greenhouse layout stays coherent.

The old watering can remains in the environment.

The original sunflower remains visible if framing allows.

Rain accumulation increases gradually.

Do not reset the floor to dry between shots.

--------------------------------------------------

[NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS]

No storyboard sheet.
No panel borders.
No panel numbers.
No captions.
No subtitles.
No timestamps.
No production notes.
No watermark.
No logos.
No brands.

No character identity drift.
No extra Lumas.
No extra Nimbus clouds.
No duplicate Sprout.
No outfit changes.
No hairstyle changes.
No missing yellow hat.
No missing flower crown after installation.

No giant Nimbus.
No black cloud.
No gray Nimbus yet.
No evil expressions.
No lightning.
No thunder.
No hurricane.
No dangerous wind.
No heavy flooding.
No destruction.
No smashed plants.
No broken greenhouse.
No injuries.

No Part 3 emotional collapse.
No exhausted Nimbus.
No Nimbus curled sadly in corner.
No Luma apology.

No magical finale.
No rainbow charm.

No warped anatomy.
No malformed hands.
No duplicated fingers.

--------------------------------------------------

[FINAL 1.8-SECOND PRIORITY]

The final beat must clearly communicate:

“The experiment worked TOO well.”

Wide sunny greenhouse.

Nimbus is slightly larger, fluffy, blue-white, wearing his flower crown.

He happily produces several gentle localized rain showers.

Plants sparkle.

Tiny puddles have appeared.

Luma stands below, looking around as multiple showers continue.

She realizes the problem.

...
